findings.issue_text: [BUG] The isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard is always False in production: spawn-context processes are multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess instances, which subclass multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess — not multiprocessing.context.Process, the sibling class that multiprocessing.Process resolves to — so process.kill() is unreachable dead code in every configuration. When _ensure_processes_alive detects a hung flusher (cause="hang"), the hung process is never killed; _create_process_for_shards spawns a replacement for the same shards, leaving two flusher processes polling the same Redis shard keys for the rest of the consumer's lifetime — doubled Redis/Kafka-producer load, and if the hung process unblocks, both processes flush the same segments and produce them to Kafka twice; every repeated hang detection leaks another process until the consumer restarts.

[BUG] The same isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check in join() is always False for both SpawnProcess and threading.Thread, so process.terminate() is unreachable and join() never terminates a flusher process that outlives its timeout. On consumer shutdown or partition rebalance, a flusher process that has not exited within the join timeout is abandoned while still running; after a rebalance it keeps flushing shards that Kafka has reassigned to another consumer, racing the new owner's flusher over the same segments.

[BUG] The time.sleep(0.1) added under the comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change" is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to lambda _: None, so the call returns instantly and yields no time to the flusher threads. The race the line was added to mitigate persists: the flusher thread can observe stopped.value = True during join() and exit before running process_stale_segments at drift 9000, leaving messages empty so (msg,) = messages raises ValueError and test_basic fails intermittently.

[ADVISORY] The diff rewrites the entire unhealthy-detection/kill/restart path in _ensure_processes_alive, but no test in the diff exercises a flusher process dying or hanging — the new test only asserts process count and shard mapping. A regression in the self-healing restart path ships silently; the unreachable process.kill() at line 253 proves the point — nothing in the suite would notice the restart mechanism being broken while spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy keeps firing.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard (singular) has zero call sites anywhere in the diff; every creation and restart path goes through _create_process_for_shards (plural). Six lines of dead code whose name differs by one character from the real restart entry point invite a future caller to invoke the wrong method; deleting it removes the ambiguity.

[ADVISORY] The new metric tags are internally inconsistent and not actually per-shard: spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce tags under key "shards" while spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes use "shard", and the value is shard_tag — the comma-joined list of every shard in the process, not an individual shard. Operators cannot filter or group these timers by shard (the tag value is a list, so only substring matching works), and dashboards joining on the shard tag — which spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy emits correctly per individual shard — silently miss the wait_produce series keyed under "shards".

[ADVISORY] flusher_processes is unvalidated with surprising falsy semantics: max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards) turns --flusher-processes 0 into one process per shard (the maximum, not the minimum), a negative value such as --flusher-processes=-3 makes num_processes negative so the empty process_to_shards_map raises KeyError in SpanFlusher.__init__, and the factory's None default (one process per shard) contradicts the CLI default of 1. An operator passing 0 or a negative value gets a silent explosion to one process per shard or a cryptic KeyError crash at consumer startup instead of a validation error, and construction paths that omit the kwarg (e.g. test_basic) run a different process topology than the production default, so the suite validates a configuration production never uses.

[BUG] The restart path gates process.kill() behind isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which is always False for the spawn-context processes this class creates (multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess subclasses multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess directly, not the context.Process shim exported as multiprocessing.Process), so unhealthy flusher processes are never killed. On a hang, _ensure_processes_alive spawns a replacement process but leaves the hung one alive: every restart leaks a live process holding Redis connections that can resume polling the same shards alongside its replacement, and repeated hangs burn through MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS until the RuntimeError consumer restart. The pre-diff code called self.process.kill() unconditionally, so this diff breaks the production (spawn) restart path while the thread-based test path — where the gate is intentionally skipped — masks the breakage entirely.

[BUG] join() gates process.terminate() behind isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which is False for spawn-context SpawnProcess instances, so flusher processes are never terminated at shutdown. Shutdown relies entirely on the shared stopped flag; a hung flusher process — the exact case terminate exists for — survives strategy shutdown and keeps polling Redis for shards that a rebalance may have already reassigned, racing with the new owner, and the new multi-process design multiplies the number of such leaked processes per consumer.

[BUG] The --flusher-processes option uses a bare click int type with no lower bound, and SpanFlusher computes num_processes = min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards)) without clamping, so any negative value silently creates zero flusher processes (range(-1) is empty). An operator passing --flusher-processes=-1 gets a consumer that writes spans to Redis and never flushes them: with self.buffers empty, submit() skips record_stored_segments, can never observe backpressure, and the memory check sees available=0 and skips rejection, so Redis grows unbounded until OOM destroys the buffered spans — with no error, log, or unhealthy metric. --flusher-processes=0 is instead treated as unset (0 or len(shards)) and fans out to one process per shard, the opposite of what the operator asked for.

[BUG] The added time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep to a lambda at its top, so the 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' comment describes synchronization that never happens. The race the line was added to fix — the flusher thread producing the segment after the drift change but before step.join() sets the stopped flag — remains, so test_basic stays flaky while the comment tells maintainers the timing was addressed; the monkeypatch also turns the flusher threads' time.sleep(1) idle path into a busy spin.

[BUG] The wait_produce timer tags its metric with the key "shards" while every sibling metric on the same flush loop uses "shard" (the produce timer at line 185, segment_size_bytes at line 195, and flusher_unhealthy at line 244). Dashboards and alerts slicing spans.buffer.flusher.* by the shard tag silently miss the wait_produce series; additionally flusher_unhealthy emits individual shard ints under "shard" while the timers emit comma-joined lists, so unhealthy events can never be correlated with the produce metrics of the process that hung.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten health-monitoring path (_ensure_processes_alive: per-process hang detection, the kill/restart sequence, and the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError) has no test anywhere in the diff — test_consumer.py covers only the happy-path flush and process-count structure, and test_flusher.py only asserts a backpressure Value. A regression in the restart logic ships green — which is exactly what happened with the isinstance kill gate at line 253, uncatchable by these tests because they run threads where the gate is deliberately skipped; the PR's headline feature (health monitoring) is entirely unverified, and a broken restart means hung flushers are never replaced, backpressure becomes permanent, and the consumer rejects all messages.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit asserts only dict structure (len(processes) == 2, total shard count == 4) and never submits a message, so the core new behavior — one process fetching and producing segments from multiple assigned shards through a subset SpansBuffer — is never executed. A bug in subset-buffer operation (e.g., SpansBuffer constructed with a shard subset fetching from the wrong keys, or a process skipping its second shard) passes CI; the first evidence would be missing or duplicated spans in production Kafka after --flusher-processes is enabled, since test_basic still exercises only the single-process path.

[ADVISORY] A single unhealthy flusher process now emits one flusher_unhealthy incr per shard it owns (for shard in shards: metrics.incr(...)), where the pre-diff code emitted exactly one event per incident. At the shipped default (one process owning every assigned shard), one hang fires len(assigned_shards) events with an identical cause, multiplying alert counts by shard count and tripping rate-based pages on a single incident; the per-shard loop adds no information because the process, not the shard, is the unit that failed.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard has no callers anywhere in the diff — restarts go through _create_process_for_shards directly from _ensure_processes_alive — and its comment ('Find which process this shard belongs to and restart that process') describes logic that lives elsewhere. Dead code with a misleading comment invites the next change to call it, and calling it would spawn a duplicate process for the shard's group without killing the existing one (the method never kills); deleting it removes nothing.

[ADVISORY] flusher_processes defaults to None at the factory, which SpanFlusher turns into one process per shard (max_processes = max_processes or len(assigned_shards)), while the CLI help documents 'Defaults to 1' — two different defaults for the same knob. Any construction path that omits the flag silently fans out to len(assigned_shards) processes and SpansBuffer instances instead of the documented single process; test_basic, which predates the option and cannot pass it, now constructs one flusher thread per assigned shard instead of the single thread it was written against — the extra step.poll() and sleep the author added to chase timing are the visible symptom of that unrequested fan-out.

[ADVISORY] Every process (re)creation constructs a fresh SpansBuffer(shards), and on restart _create_process_for_shards replaces self.buffers[process_index] without closing the discarded buffer — the pre-diff design reused the single factory-created buffer across all restarts. Each hang/crash restart cycle abandons a buffer (and whatever Redis client state it holds) to garbage collection and builds a replacement in both the parent (used by submit's record_stored_segments/get_memory_info calls) and the spawned child; repeated restarts up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS churn connection resources that the old design never touched.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds a generic Python union-narrowing style example (hasattr vs isinstance on str | None) to CLAUDE.md that traces to no requirement of the span buffer multiprocess/health-monitoring change. A repo-wide style-guide edit owned by dev-infra rides inside a Kafka consumer PR, so reverting or bisecting the span-buffer work drags the doc change with it and the CLAUDE.md change ships without its own review; nothing in this diff even uses hasattr.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code: no call site exists anywhere in the diff or the file — the restart path in _ensure_processes_alive calls _create_process_for_shards directly. The next maintainer assumes a per-shard restart API exists and maintains or calls a method that is never invoked; the six-line method plus its shard-lookup loop are deletable, and it is leftover implementation work from an abandoned per-shard restart design that no requirement asks for.

[ADVISORY] The constructor default (flusher_processes=None → max_processes = len(assigned_shards), one process per shard) contradicts the shipped CLI default (--flusher-processes default=1 in consumers/__init__.py, one process for all shards), and the class docstring added in this diff asserts "Creates one process per shard", which is false for the only production entry point. Any caller constructing the factory without flusher_processes (as the diff's own tests already do) silently spawns one process — each holding its own Redis client and Kafka producer — per partition, and an engineer capacity-planning from the docstring predicts N flusher processes when production runs 1.

[BUG] flusher_processes is never validated: 0 falls through `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and silently yields the maximum (one process per shard), and a negative value makes num_processes negative so range(num_processes) produces an empty map and the modulo distribution loop raises KeyError at construction. An operator passing --flusher-processes=0 gets the opposite of a minimum — one producer-and-Redis-client-bearing process per partition on every consumer — and a negative typo crashloops the consumer at startup with an opaque KeyError instead of a clear flag-validation error.

[BUG] The wait_produce timer is tagged tags={"shards": shard_tag} while the produce timer (line 185) and segment_size_bytes timing (lines 192-195) added in the same method use the key "shard", so the wait_produce key is a typo. Dashboards and alerts grouping spans.buffer.flusher.* metrics by shard silently omit the wait_produce series, splitting flush-latency observability across two tag keys and breaking any per-tag aggregation the health-monitoring intent promises.

[ADVISORY] shard_tag is a comma-joined list of the process's shard group, so under the production default of one flusher process the tag value is the consumer's entire partition assignment, a string that changes on every rebalance. spans.buffer.flusher.produce, segment_size_bytes, and wait_produce accumulate an unbounded set of distinct tag values as assignments churn (metrics-pipeline cardinality growth) while delivering zero per-shard signal — per-shard health is only actually observable on the flusher_unhealthy counter, so the stated per-shard monitoring intent is not enforced for the latency/size metrics.

[BUG] join(timeout) breaks out of the process loop as soon as the deadline has passed, skipping process.terminate() for the current and all remaining processes, where the old code always reached terminate() after its wait loop. On a shutdown that hits the timeout, all but at most the first flusher child are never terminated — hung children (the exact 'hang' case terminate exists for) keep their Redis poll loops and Kafka producers alive until the parent finally exits — and if the deadline is already expired on loop entry, not even the first process is terminated.

[BUG] The added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to lambda _: None, so the "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change" comment describes synchronization that never happens. The race the line was added to fix — the flusher thread must observe the new current_drift before step.join() sets the stopped flag — remains unfixed, so test_basic still fails intermittently when the thread exits before producing, and future maintainers trust a mitigation that provably does nothing.

[ADVISORY] The diff rewrites _ensure_process_alive into per-process-group restart machinery (per-group restart counters, isinstance kill guard, recreate-with-same-shards, per-group RuntimeError threshold) but no test added or updated in this diff drives a process unhealthy, triggers a restart, or reaches MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS. A regression in the rewritten restart path — e.g., a per-group counter that never increments or a recreate using a stale shard map — silently stops flushing one shard group, letting segments accumulate in Redis until backpressure rejects ingestion, with no failing test anywhere in the diff to catch it.

[ADVISORY] The parent retains one SpansBuffer per process group in self.buffers whose only reads are the record_stored_segments and get_memory_info loops in submit(), duplicating shard coverage that the full-shard buffer passed into the constructor already provides over the disjoint groups. With flusher_processes > 1 the parent holds N redundant Redis-client-bearing buffer objects where one suffices, every process restart constructs a fresh SpansBuffer and orphans the previous one's connection pool to garbage collection, and the codebase gains a second shard-to-buffer mapping that must be kept consistent with process_to_shards_map on every change.

[BUG] join(timeout) never terminates any flusher process it reaches after the deadline has expired, because the `break` on the remaining_time check exits the for-loop before the `process.terminate()` at the bottom of the loop body runs. Whenever join is called with a timeout that next_step.join or a slow first process consumes, every remaining flusher process is left un-terminated: a hung flusher child keeps polling Redis and producing to Kafka after the strategy is considered shut down, and on a rebalance (where the consumer keeps running) it competes with the replacement strategy's flushers over the same shards until the consumer process finally exits; the old single-process code always ran terminate().

[BUG] The wait_produce timer is tagged with key "shards" while the produce timer (line 185) and the segment_size_bytes timing (lines 192-196) tag the identical shard_tag value under key "shard". Dashboards, alerts, and queries that aggregate flusher metrics by the shard dimension silently miss every spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce series (a `shard=...` filter returns nothing for it), so produce time and produce-wait time cannot be compared per shard or per process group.

[BUG] In pipe mode the flusher runs as a threading.Thread, which the isinstance guard makes un-killable, so a hang restart in _ensure_processes_alive spawns a replacement thread for the same shards while the hung original keeps running, and both threads write the same shared process_healthy_since[process_index] and process_backpressure_since[process_index] Values. After any hang-restart in the multiprocessing-consumer (pipe) deployment, two flusher threads concurrently poll and produce the same Redis shards (doubled Redis load and duplicate producers per worker), and the replacement's healthy_since writes permanently mask a genuinely hung thread from ever being re-detected; threads accumulate one per restart until MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS kills the consumer.

[ADVISORY] flusher_processes is never validated: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` converts 0 into one-process-per-shard (maximum parallelism), and any negative value makes num_processes negative so `range(num_processes)` yields an empty process_to_shards_map while the distribution loop computes `i % -1 == 0` and raises KeyError on `self.process_to_shards_map[0]`. An operator who sets --flusher-processes 0 expecting to minimize or disable the flusher silently gets maximum parallelism (one flusher child with its own Kafka producer and Redis pool per shard in non-pipe mode), and a negative typo crash-loops the consumer at startup or rebalance with an opaque KeyError deep in SpanFlusher.__init__.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard is dead code: no caller exists anywhere in this diff, since _ensure_processes_alive restarts via _create_process_for_shards directly. Six lines of never-executed, untested code whose singular name promises shard-granular restart while it actually restarts the entire process group; the next contributor either calls it believing the name or has to rediscover the real restart path, and it will rot unexercised.

[ADVISORY] The same knob has two conflicting defaults: the CLI option passes flusher_processes=1 (one flusher total), while the constructor default None makes SpanFlusher fall back to one process per shard via `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. Any programmatic construction that omits flusher_processes (as the updated test_basic already does) silently runs one flusher child per shard — multiplying Kafka producers, Redis pools, and restart/backpressure semantics — instead of the "Defaults to 1" behavior the help text documents, with no signal that the entry paths diverge.

[ADVISORY] submit() routes record_stored_segments() (and get_memory_info() at lines 298-300) through the flusher's own per-process SpansBuffer copies even though the buffer passed to the constructor covers the identical shards and these are Redis-mediated operations, so the parent keeps one extra live buffer — each holding its own Redis client/pool — per flusher process purely for bookkeeping. The parent consumer's Redis connection and memory footprint now scales with --flusher-processes for calls the original buffer already serves, and the duplicated construction site (SpansBuffer(shards) at line 94) drifts independently of the factory's buffer construction, so any future constructor configuration added at one site is silently absent at the other and the write path and flush path operate on differently-configured buffers.

[ADVISORY] shard_tag joins all of a process's shard ids into one comma-separated string used as a single "shard" tag value, so under the shipped default (--flusher-processes 1, one process handling every shard) the tag value is the full list "0,1,2,...". The newly added shard tags on the produce and segment_size metrics cannot be filtered per shard in the default configuration and cannot be joined with the individual-shard tags on flusher_unhealthy, and the embedded commas collide with the delimiter statsd/dogstatsd uses to separate tags, corrupting the serialized tag list sent to the metrics backend.

[ADVISORY] Per-process state is spread across six parallel dicts keyed by process_index (processes, buffers, process_to_shards_map, process_healthy_since, process_backpressure_since, process_restarts) that must be kept in lockstep, and the restart path already updates only a subset of them while the rest are init-only. The next change that adds, removes, or re-keys a flusher process must touch six synchronized maps; missing one (e.g. replacing processes[i] without the matching healthy_since reset, or extending restart to a new map) silently desyncs health or backpressure tracking with no failing test, and a per-process dataclass would collapse all six into one structure.

[BUG] SpanFlusher.terminate() — the method directly following join() in this file, untouched by this diff — still references the self.process attribute that this diff deletes (the last updated reference is the isinstance/terminate pair at the end of join()), so arroyo's terminate() call raises AttributeError. Every consumer shutdown or partition revocation that calls terminate() crashes the ingest-spans consumer with AttributeError instead of stopping its flusher processes, leaving spawn processes running that still hold old shard assignments and can flush segments after those shards are reassigned, producing duplicate span payloads in Kafka.

[BUG] The added time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches time.sleep to lambda _: None at its top, so the wait the new comment promises ("Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") never happens. The drift-then-join race the line was added to fix remains: join() sets the stopped flag before the flusher thread has flushed the pending segment, so `(msg,) = messages` can intermittently fail to unpack and the test flakes in CI exactly as before the supposed fix.

[BUG] join()'s `if remaining_time <= 0: break` exits the for-loop before the terminate() call at the loop bottom is reached, so every flusher process after the one that exhausted the deadline is left neither waited on nor terminated, whereas the original code unconditionally terminated its process after the wait loop. When join(timeout) expires while a flusher process is hung during a rebalance (where the consumer process keeps running), the remaining hung spawn processes are never SIGTERM'd and keep polling Redis and producing for shards already reassigned to another consumer, yielding duplicate span payloads in Kafka.

[BUG] The new --flusher-processes knob is unvalidated end to end: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats an explicit 0 as unset and silently spawns one process per shard, and any negative value makes `i % self.num_processes` index into the empty process_to_shards_map (range(-1) is empty), raising KeyError. An operator passing --flusher-processes 0 gets the maximum process count — the opposite of the option's "Maximum number of processes" contract — and an operator passing any negative value crashes the consumer at startup with a bare KeyError instead of a validation error.

[BUG] The wait_produce timer is tagged with key "shards" while the sibling produce timer and segment_size_bytes timing use "shard" for the same shard_tag value, splitting the metric series across two different tag keys. Dashboards and alerts for spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce that group or filter by the shard tag — as the sibling metrics use — silently match nothing, so per-shard produce-wait latency is unmonitorable.

[ADVISORY] shard_tag is a comma-joined list of every shard a process handles and is used as the tag value on spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes, while spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy tags individual shard ids. With the default single-process configuration the tag enumerates the consumer's entire shard assignment (useless for per-shard diagnosis), and as Kafka rebalances change assignments the set of distinct tag values grows without bound, inflating metrics cardinality in the statsd backend; SREs also cannot correlate these joined-list tags with the per-shard flusher_unhealthy alerts this PR adds.

[ADVISORY] test_flusher_processes_limit, the only test that constructs a multi-process flusher, asserts only dict sizes (len(flusher.processes) == 2, shard-count sums) and joins without ever submitting a message or asserting any produced output, so no test verifies data actually flows through more than one flusher process. A regression in the new multi-process path — per-shard SpansBuffer wiring, shared stopped/current_drift handling across processes, per-process backpressure rejection in submit(), or the _ensure_processes_alive restart path — ships silently and first manifests in production as lost or duplicate spans or wrong offset commits instead of a CI failure.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard has no callers anywhere in this diff, and its body delegates to _create_process_for_shards, which overwrites self.processes[process_index] without stopping or joining the process it replaces. The method is dead code today, but the first maintainer to wire it up (its comment advertises "restart that process") silently leaves the replaced process running alongside its replacement, creating two flushers for the same shards and duplicate span payloads to Kafka; it should be deleted or fixed to stop the old process first.

[BUG] The new flusher_processes value reaches SpanFlusher arithmetic unvalidated: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` coerces 0 to one-process-per-shard, and a negative value makes `range(num_processes)` empty so `process_to_shards_map[i % num_processes]` raises KeyError during construction. An operator running `--flusher-processes=0` on a many-shard deployment silently spawns one flusher process per shard — each with its own Redis connections and Kafka producer — instead of the intended limit, and any negative value crash-loops the consumer at startup with an unhandled KeyError instead of a config error; the click option in src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py declares only type=int with no min bound.

[BUG] SpanFlusher.join breaks out of the process loop as soon as the deadline expires, skipping the terminate() call for every process not yet reached, so those flusher processes are never terminated. With flusher-processes > 1 and a shutdown/rebalance deadline consumed while waiting on the first process, the remaining flusher processes keep polling Redis and producing to Kafka after join() returns — overlapping with the new partition owner's flusher for the same shards (duplicate flush work and, if the Redis segment flush is not atomic, duplicate span production) and holding Redis/Kafka resources until the main process exits; the code being replaced always terminated its process after the wait window.

[BUG] The wait_produce timer emits the shard dimension under tag key "shards" while the produce timer and segment_size_bytes timing emit the identical shard_tag value under key "shard". The spans.buffer.flusher.* metric family splits across two tag keys, so dashboards and alerts that group or correlate these timers by shard silently drop every wait_produce series, and the dimension cannot be joined with spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy (which tags individual shard ids).

[ADVISORY] shard_tag joins all of a process's shard ids into one comma-separated string that is used as the value of a metric tag on produce, segment_size_bytes, and wait_produce. With the default flusher-processes=1 the tag enumerates the consumer's entire partition assignment, producing a near-unique value per deployment that multiplies series on every rebalance and defeats shard-level aggregation; the embedded commas are also the statsd tag separator, so comma-splitting backends parse a value like shard:0,1,2 as tag shard:0 followed by bogus tags 1 and 2.

[ADVISORY] _create_process_for_shard (singular) is unreachable — no call site exists in this diff; both _create_processes and _ensure_processes_alive invoke the plural _create_process_for_shards. Six lines of dead restart logic ship in the flusher and mislead the next maintainer: invoking it to restart one shard actually restarts the entire process group sharing that shard; deleting it removes the confusion with no behavior change.

[ADVISORY] Per-process state is spread across six parallel dicts keyed by process_index (processes, buffers, process_to_shards_map, process_healthy_since, process_backpressure_since, process_restarts) that must be mutated in lockstep by __init__, _create_process_for_shards, _ensure_processes_alive, and submit. The next per-process change (a new counter, a new Value, a new restart policy) must update all six structures correctly across four methods; a missed dict yields a KeyError or silently stale state — e.g. a field initialized in __init__ but not refreshed on the restart path would silently skip per-process bookkeeping; a single ProcessState dataclass holding process, buffer, shards, and the mp_context.Values makes the invariant unbreakable.

[ADVISORY] The new process-recovery path — _ensure_processes_alive detecting a dead or hung process, killing it, recreating it via _create_process_for_shards, incrementing process_restarts, and raising RuntimeError at MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS — is executed by no test in this diff. A regression in the restart path (stale self.processes entry, healthy_since not reset, restarts never incrementing, or the join terminate-skip) silently disables the self-healing that this PR's health-monitoring claim rests on and ships undetected; the diff's own thread-mode (produce_to_pipe) tests make kill/recreate deterministic to exercise.

[BUG] The `time.sleep(0.1)` added to test_basic to "give flusher threads time to process after drift change" is a no-op, because the same test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at its start, so the wait the comment describes never happens. The race the change was meant to fix — flusher threads not having fetched/produced the segment before `step.join()` sets the stopped flag — is not addressed: the test's pass depends on the incidental wall-time of the added `step.poll()`, leaving test_basic prone to intermittent `(msg,) = messages` ValueError failures in CI while the comment tells maintainers the timing was handled.

[BUG] test_flusher_processes_limit verifies only constructor bookkeeping — `len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes`, and a shard-count sum — and never submits a message, asserts any production, or checks process liveness, so it passes even if every flusher process crashes on startup (thread exceptions are swallowed by threading's default excepthook). The shared-shards flushing mode — one flusher process handling multiple shards, which is exactly what the new `--flusher-processes` CLI option's default of 1 runs in production — has zero behavioral verification: a regression in `SpanFlusher.main`'s new `shards` handling or in per-shard-group `SpansBuffer` construction ships CI-green; the `total_shards == 4` assertion also passes on a mis-distribution that assigns one shard twice and drops another, and the `commits` list is collected but never asserted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When the flusher runs in thread mode (`produce_to_pipe` set, as in both tests in this diff and in pipe-mode deployments), the restart path never stops the old thread because `process.kill()` is guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, so a hang-restart leaves the old thread alive alongside its replacement, both polling the same Redis shards. If the "hung" thread un-sticks (e.g. the produce pipe drains), two flushers concurrently fetch the same shards — violating the one-flusher-per-shard invariant the shard mapping enforces — causing duplicated segment fetches and potentially duplicate span payloads produced to Kafka; the old thread also keeps writing the shared `process_healthy_since[process_index]` Value, masking the replacement thread's health.
